hints: Region A lies between the curve $y = 4(3x+4)^{1/2} - 2x - 6$ and the axes, from $x=0$ to $x=7$.
Integrate $4(3x+4)^{1/2}$ using reverse chain rule: $\int 4(3x+4)^{1/2} dx = 4 \times \frac{(3x+4)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 3} = \frac{8}{9}(3x+4)^{3/2}$.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral for region A between the curve and the axes from $x = 0$ to $x = 7$:
$$\text{Area}(A) = \int_0^7 \left(4(3x+4)^{1/2} - 2x - 6\right) dx$$

Integrate each term using the reverse chain rule on $(3x+4)^{1/2}$:
$$\int 4(3x+4)^{1/2} dx = 4 \times \frac{(3x+4)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 3} = \frac{8}{9}(3x+4)^{3/2}, \quad \int (-2x - 6) dx = -x^2 - 6x$$

Evaluate the antiderivative $\left[\frac{8}{9}(3x+4)^{3/2} - x^2 - 6x\right]$ at limits $7$ and $0$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{At } x = 7: &\quad \frac{8}{9}(25)^{3/2} - 7^2 - 6(7) = \frac{8}{9}(125) - 91 = \frac{1000}{9} - 91 = \frac{181}{9} \\ \text{At } x = 0: &\quad \frac{8}{9}(4)^{3/2} - 0 = \frac{8}{9}(8) = \frac{64}{9} \end{aligned}$$

Subtract the lower limit value to obtain the exact area of region A:
$$\text{Area}(A) = \frac{181}{9} - \frac{64}{9} = \frac{117}{9} = 13$$

hints: Differentiate $y = 4(3x+4)^{1/2} - 2x - 6$ using the chain rule to find $\frac{dy}{dx} = 6(3x+4)^{-1/2} - 2$.
Evaluate $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $P(7,0)$ to get the tangent gradient $m = -\frac{4}{5}$, and write the tangent line equation $y = -\frac{4}{5}x + \frac{28}{5}$.
Find the $y$-intercept $Q\left(0, \frac{28}{5}\right)$, and calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $OPQ$ under the tangent line: $\frac{1}{2}(7)\left(\frac{28}{5}\right) = \frac{98}{5}$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the curve equation using the chain rule:
$$y = 4(3x+4)^{1/2} - 2x - 6 \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = 4 \times \frac{1}{2}(3x+4)^{-1/2}(3) - 2 = \frac{6}{\sqrt{3x+4}} - 2$$

Evaluate the gradient at $P(7, 0)$ and form the tangent equation:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=7} = \frac{6}{5} - 2 = -\frac{4}{5} \implies y - 0 = -\frac{4}{5}(x - 7) \implies y = -\frac{4}{5}x + \frac{28}{5}$$

Find the $y$-intercept $Q\left(0, \frac{28}{5}\right)$ and calculate the area of right triangle $OPQ$ under the tangent line:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle OPQ) = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times \frac{28}{5} = \frac{98}{5} = 19.6$$

Subtract the area of region A ($13$) from the triangle area to find the area of region B:
$$\text{Area}(B) = \text{Area}(\triangle OPQ) - \text{Area}(A) = \frac{98}{5} - 13 = \frac{98 - 65}{5} = \frac{33}{5} = 6.6$$
